Prepared 5 November 2026; submission recorded separately in the protocol and ledger. Base commit `2f0f534e8311ee597e516b11c2afca1bbf608060`, bot `leader_party_tuned`. Copy only to `bots/pi_safe-dash-wake-01/`; edit only that candidate and write `IMPLEMENTATION.md`. PC builds/tests the exact returned source. Do not inherit any prior candidate, upload, challenge, or change ranked selection.

## Evidence and exact scope

Original Swirl/C02/B Heart599,864,985 has locally visible sleeping hit camps, all surviving group members visible and legal zero-current-exposure ordinary moves. Fresh local/source facts support escape in allthree.599's two directly hit elk receive stun1 and cause no attack before nextturn.864 hits/stuns34 but wakes unstunned38 outside radius1, causing54HP damage at865.985 hits/stuns52/54 and kills passive101, but wakes48/50 outside radius1; their attacks consume108 existing shield, not HP. Original A1637 kills passive56 and wakes four damaging members outside radius1;1646 hits/stuns61 but wakes15/67/69 outside radius1. All relevant members are locally visible. The earlier death also includes an ally-wake recall interruption; **do not implement that separate hypothesis**.

Sources: [three-case local audit](../low-health-dash-local.md), [carrier local audit](../carrier-loss-local.md), [frozen fixture inputs](../sdw01-fixture-inputs.json), [design](../safe-dash-witness-design.md), [resource comparison](../safe-dash-resource-admission.md). Only change the chosen `safe=true`, unconstrained dash decision in `move_to`. Preserve original field/mask construction, goal choice, ordinary-step ranking, dash-endpoint ranking, distance-improvement threshold, ready checks, action priority and unsafe/constrained behavior, except unavoidable added query/epoch-check costs. No extra field, alternate-dash search, new path planner, new task/retreat threshold, gold recall, shop/draft or banking change.

## Small immutable topology seam

Avoid `camp.camp_group()` in the movement hot path. Exact SDK-wrapper native measurement finds8â€“13host calls per deduplicated hit group in these cases; cached membership lookup uses zero hostcalls. Actual game fuel is unmeasured.

Provide a small immutable `CampTopologyView` (or equivalent narrow type) over the groups already owned by `World.camps`. It may hold a `const World*` with its membership accessor defined where World is complete, or an equivalent borrowed immutable view. Expose only identityâ†’group-member identities, not objective lifecycle/progress or live hidden state. A missing identity must be explicit, not an invented empty/passive group. Do not build a second persistent cache or reload all groups. World initialization already loads groups and sorts objectives before movement; no group-vector mutation may occur while the view/member span is in use.

Construct/use the view synchronously after `World::init`; never store it or member spans in Memory, static state, deferred work or callbacks. Returned member spans refer to existing World-owned group storage. If a view wrapper is passed by value, it must remain a non-owning lightweight view. Forward the same view through `retreatâ†’move_to` and the hidden-blocker recursive `move_to(...,constrained=true)`. Update every caller: Bot camp/guard paths, escape/retreat, carrier protection, bank and explore. Each already has World available. Unsafe/constrained callers still preserve their former actions and skip this witness policy. Do not pass a temporary copied World/container whose spans would dangle.

## Chosen-endpoint witness

Reuse one captured `vision::camps()` list already needed by safe-mask construction. Record current member identity/state/position; reuse state reads rather than repeat alive/awake queries. Reuse Strength/range already obtained for awake mask members; query sleeping-member Strength/range lazily only when needed for a hit group. Wrapper objects are live getters, not snapshots. Never query live state through an unseen group member handle; intersect static member identities with this captured visible list.

Scope this first variant to a dash with **positive damage modifier/current damage and positive stun duration**, using its documented common landing damage/stun radius. Zero-damage and zero-stun dashes preserve original behavior; no unsupported broader prediction. For the original chosen endpoint:

- Find visible living camps within landing radius. If none, preserve the dash without topology lookup.
- Resolve only those hit groups through the immutable view, deduplicating by cached member identities/group identity. Hitting an awake member or killing a passive member may still wake sleeping siblings; do not require the hit member or whole group asleep.
- A veto witness is a currently visible, living, sleeping, positive-Strength member of a hit group, **outside landing radius**, whose current attack range covers the landing. It survives this dash by geometry; exact camp damage/capping is unnecessary for that member. Directly hit/stunned members do not satisfy this initial predicate.
- First witness skips the dash and falls through to the existing ordinary `best` move. Do not search alternate endpoints, change `mem.blocked`/`last_distance` before actual movement, or grant another field. A complete scan without a visible witness preserves the original dash.

Whole passive groups, already-awake damaging members alone, directly stunned599-style members and out-of-reach sleeping members therefore retain original behavior. Hidden members are not queried or treated as automatic vetoes; no-visible-witness is not omniscient safety. A static identity missing from the initialized topology is an incomplete check, not a negative result.

## Explicit resource contract

The first experimental admission is `fuel_remaining() >= 15000` at the start of the chosen-endpoint witness (10000 above the existing5000 action reserve). **15000 is a fixed experimental bound, not a measured necessary/sufficient fuel cost.** Do not tune it on the screen. A native mock cannot establish game fuel. Record admission and incremental host-query costs in diagnostic testing.

Check epoch/reserve during the new capture/query work and immediately before action. Under admission but same epoch with action reserve intact: skip the dash and fall through to the existing ordinary move. If a witness check runs short but remains current/above reserve, likewise ordinary fallback. If the epoch changed or fuel falls below action reserve, return deferred with no dash and no stale ordinary action. Distinguish resource fallback from camp-witness veto in native diagnostics. Check after each new host-backed query; do not knowingly continue a stale scan. The pre-field safe-mask capture must abort on rollover before building a field. Preserve the existing field admission/field count rules.

No `camp_group()` host loader, repeated vision collection per endpoint, group-state query, hidden live query or persistent live cache. Do not claim identical inactive artifact trajectories: reduced duplicate getters and new checks may change fuel even when the policy does not veto. Do not add release logs; use native diagnostics and existing100-round telemetry. Any temporary instrumented binary is separate and cannot stand in for release evidence.

Same map/action with all relevant members awake, pure passive group, sleeping threat just beyond attack reach, no hit, zero damage, zero stun, safe=false or constrained=true preserves the appropriate original action. Exact attack-range/radius boundaries matter. An awake hit member with a sleeping sibling and a killed passive hit member can still veto.
3. An invisible member's live-query stub throws if called; hidden members are never queried. A mixed group may still have a visible witness. Multiple hit members in one group and multiple hit groups resolve correctly without any group-loader hostcalls. Missing topology returns incomplete.
4. Low admission/current epoch uses ordinary fallback; below reserve or simulated rollover at each new host query issues no action. A rollover must not return to retreat and move from stale facts. Check public movement/retreat behavior, not just helper return values.
5. Forwarding through every public caller and recursive constrained retry preserves view lifetime and unchanged fallback. Copying/reallocation is prohibited while spans are active. No extra field, selector reset, priority/Memory transition or release log. Invoke ordinary path failure/retry as well as success.

List mocked host geometry/fuel/combat limitations. Run SDK syntax/build checks and the native fixture with warnings enabled. No full matches on Pi. Provide exact commands, source hashes, results and deviations in IMPLEMENTATION.md. Explain an unmet contract instead of weakening it.
